A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MotionBench and TE Fusion work. Their complete 20-page contents, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MotionBench evaluations, compression experiments across four benchmarks, and error analyses in Section 5 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations, compression results, and error analyses, including Tables 3, 4, 7, and 8.

M1.justification: TE Fusion retains grouped attention across neighboring frames followed by spatiotemporal downsampling. Section 8 adds tensor shapes and a 3D-convolution specification as implementation explanations, without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: The reported training datasets, MotionBench's six tasks and 5,385 videos/8,052 questions, and evaluation coverage across MotionBench, MVBench, LVBench, and Video-MME are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the same model comparisons. The compression experiments retain the uncompressed baseline, QFormer, Qwen2-VL, PLLaVA, Kangaroo, and TE Fusion in Tables 4, 7, and 8.

E3.justification: Reported splits, frame counts, compression sweeps, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged. The new answer-parsing and response-prompt paragraph documents previously unspecified details of the existing evaluation; it does not establish a revised protocol or rerun.

E4.justification: The compression-ratio analyses, all-model failure breakdown, and hand-on-car error case are retained. Moving and renumbering the appendix's experimental-results and case-study sections does not add analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the evaluations. Point-estimate reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries in Tables 3, 4, 7, and 8 are unchanged, including TE Fusion's 0.58 dev and test accuracies in Table 3. Compression curves, error-category plots, and qualitative findings are also retained.

T1.justification: The new tensor equations in Section 8 re-express the existing grouped-attention and downsampling computation. The annotation-density definition and decoder-length relation remain unchanged; no distinct theoretical result, assumption, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution, diagnosis of weak motion understanding, and claims about TE Fusion under compression. The new appendix originality section elaborates existing contribution positioning.

C2.justification: Section 11 newly argues that reusing existing annotations offers little incremental information and risks training-data leakage. Existing interpretations of model failures and MotionBench's geographic, cultural, and annotation-error limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds the response instruction, first-uppercase-letter extraction rule, and TE Fusion tensor shapes and convolution parameters. It removes the shared forward-pass pseudocode, including its explicit absolute temporal-position-embedding detail. Training hyperparameters and data-access provisions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Section 11 explicitly contrasts MotionBench with MVBench on source diversity, reuse of annotations, and human correction versus rule-based construction. This sharpens research positioning without changing the cited-work set.

P1.justification: v2 removes the stray drafting sentence in related work, corrects an introductory figure reference, adds funding acknowledgments, and expands the model explanation. Copyright information moves to the appendix, whose subsequent sections are renumbered; the main narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: Table 5 receives a conventional caption, Table 6 moves to the following appendix page, and the pseudocode panel is removed, producing local reflow. Figures and result-table contents are retained, and page-number footers disappear.

improvement.justification: Explicit answer extraction and clearer tensor/downsampling documentation improve reproducibility and understanding, while editorial and caption corrections improve readability. Removing the shared pseudocode loses some implementation detail, limiting the gain. The empirical evidence and central conclusions remain unchanged.
